cohort: The study enrolled 100 pregnant women, 50 with idiopathic oligohydramnios (AFI <=5) and 50 gestational age-matched controls with normal AFI (5-25 cm), diagnosed between 34-40 weeks of gestation.
finding: Isolated oligohydramnios is associated with increased obstetric interventions, higher caesarean rates, and adverse neonatal outcomes, including SGA and higher NICU admissions, despite reassuring antenatal fetal surveillance.
mod_finding: The study found markedly higher caesarean section rates in the oligohydramnios group (78% vs. 32%), primarily due to fetal distress.
